      "body": "uniqueGuests uses strict equality against existing attendee emails and does not lowercase/normalize guest emails. It also does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array. This allows duplicate attendee rows via case variations such as a@example.com and A@example.com, and it can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS because the blacklist is lowercased while the incoming guest email is not."

      "body": "The handler only checks that the booking exists and that the caller has permission. It does not reject cancelled or rejected bookings, and it does not consider whether the booking is in a state where adding guests is valid. API callers can therefore add guests to cancelled bookings and send incorrect emails/calendar updates."
    },

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Emails are sent for the original guests array instead of the guests actually added",
      "body": "After filtering to uniqueGuests and inserting only those attendees, the handler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). sendAddGuestsEmails uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide whether an attendee receives a full invite or an add-guest notification. If the request includes an existing attendee together with at least one new guest, the existing attendee will be treated as newly added and receive the wrong email. The handler should pass uniqueGuests, ideally normalized."

findings.title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of admin OR owner
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). The name and intended authorization logic imply that a team admin or team owner should be allowed. With &&, a team admin who is not an owner is denied, and depending on how isTeamOwner/isTeamAdmin classify roles, even some owners could be denied. This blocks legitimate team users from adding guests.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
findings.body: The handler grants permission if the authenticated user's email matches any attendee email on the booking. This means an invited guest who has a Cal.com account can add arbitrary additional guests, trigger emails, and update calendar attendees. Unless this is an explicit product decision, guest-management should be restricted to the organizer/host/team admins.

findings.title: Guest emails are not normalized or deduplicated before insert
findings.body: uniqueGuests uses strict equality against existing attendee emails and does not lowercase/normalize guest emails. It also does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array. This allows duplicate attendee rows via case variations such as a@example.com and A@example.com, and it can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS because the blacklist is lowercased while the incoming guest email is not.

findings.title: Booking status is not validated before adding guests
findings.body: The handler only checks that the booking exists and that the caller has permission. It does not reject cancelled or rejected bookings, and it does not consider whether the booking is in a state where adding guests is valid. API callers can therefore add guests to cancelled bookings and send incorrect emails/calendar updates.

findings.title: Emails are sent for the original guests array instead of the guests actually added
findings.body: After filtering to uniqueGuests and inserting only those attendees, the handler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). sendAddGuestsEmails uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide whether an attendee receives a full invite or an add-guest notification. If the request includes an existing attendee together with at least one new guest, the existing attendee will be treated as newly added and receive the wrong email. The handler should pass uniqueGuests, ideally normalized.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email disable settings
findings.body: Unlike other email-sending helpers, sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept eventTypeMetadata and does not check eventTypeDisableHostEmail or eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Add-guests emails will therefore be sent even when the event type is configured to disable standard host or attendee emails.

findings.title: No maximum length for guests array
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an arbitrary-length array of email addresses. An authenticated user could submit thousands of guest emails, causing bulk database writes and mass email sending. Add a reasonable maximum length to the guests array.

findings.title: Attendee creation is not atomic with the existing-attendee check
findings.body: The handler reads booking.attendees, filters guests, then creates attendees in a separate update. There is no transaction or database-level uniqueness check preventing the same guest from being added by concurrent requests. Two simultaneous addGuests calls for the same email can both pass the filter and create duplicate attendee rows.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking owner's credentials
findings.body: The handler fetches booking.user.credentials but then constructs EventManager with ctx.user and credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). If a team admin or attendee who is not the booking owner adds guests, the requester may not own the calendar credential associated with the booking, so updateCalendarAttendees may fail or update the wrong calendar. The calendar update should use the booking owner/host credentials or the credential associated with the booking reference.

findings.title: Team member add-guests email is rendered with the organizer as the attendee
findings.body: OrganizerAddGuestsEmail can be sent to a team member via this.teamMember?.email, but renderEmail is called with attendee: this.calEvent.organizer. Any recipient-specific rendering such as greeting, locale, timezone, or time format may use the organizer instead of the actual team-member recipient. It should pass this.teamMember || this.calEvent.organizer.

findings.title: Closing the dialog via onOpenChange does not reset form state
findings.body: AddGuestsDialog passes onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}, which only toggles visibility. Closing via overlay or Escape does not reset multiEmailValue or isInvalidEmail; only the Cancel button does. Reopening the dialog can show stale emails or stale validation errors.

findings.title: Validation error state is not cleared after a later valid submission
findings.body: When validation fails, isInvalidEmail is set to true, but when a later submission validates successfully and calls addGuestsMutation.mutate, isInvalidEmail is not set back to false. If the mutation succeeds and the dialog is reopened, the validation error may be displayed before the user has done anything invalid.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and may display undefined
findings.body: The error handler builds message as a template string: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. Because the template string is always truthy, the fallback t(unable_to_add_guests) is never used. If err.data?.code is undefined, users may see a toast beginning with undefined. Build the message conditionally.
